purpose: Define REST, OSC, WebSocket, WebRTC and other protocol services as explicit installable/removable capabilities rather than implicit mandatory runtime semantics, except where an owning profile/use-case explicitly requires them.

topics.name: Protocol Optionality
topics.purpose: Define REST, OSC, WebSocket, WebRTC and other protocol services as explicit installable/removable capabilities rather than implicit mandatory runtime semantics, except where an owning profile/use-case explicitly requires them.

semantics.default_rule: Protocol capability existence is explicit and profile/config driven.
semantics.dependency_rule: A consumer requiring a protocol declares that dependency and hard-fails when absent; runtime never auto-enables it.
semantics.removal_rule: Removing a protocol capability must expose dependent consumers as invalid/unavailable rather than silently substituting another protocol.
semantics.fallback_rule: Protocol fallback requires explicit semantic policy.
semantics.authority_rule: Enabling a protocol does not grant operation/data authority.
semantics.core_rule: Core semantic model is not defined by the presence of any optional protocol binding.

invariants.rule: Network identity, transport, remote authority and payload semantics remain explicit and separate.

hard_gates.condition: protocol silently substituted by another transport
dependent consumer remains marked valid when required protocol absent
optional protocol treated as universal Core semantic requirement
protocol presence inferred from listener/file existence only

references.purpose: Protocol capability presence follows explicit boot/profile semantics.
Protocol capability existence is separate from authority.

prose.summary: Define REST, OSC, WebSocket, WebRTC and other protocol services as explicit installable/removable capabilities rather than implicit mandatory runtime semantics, except where an owning profile/use-case explicitly requires them.
